speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and has it been getting worse since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a forceful avulsion injury. Can you describe the nature of the pain, and are you able to actively bend or straighten the tip of the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: This presentation is classic for a "Jersey Finger" injury, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of Right Ring Finger Flexor Tendon

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound was normal, I suspect the injury is bony rather than purely tendinous. Can you point me to the exact spot of maximum tenderness, and have you noticed any bruising or deformity at the tip of the finger? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Ring Finger

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray and ultrasound are negative for fracture or tendon avulsion, we must consider a joint injury. Can you actively extend the middle joint of your finger, and does the finger feel unstable or wobbly when you try to move it? REQUEST TEST: MRI Right Hand and Wrist

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Preliminary findings expected to show details regarding the integrity of tendons.

speaker: Doctor
text: While we wait for the MRI, can you tell me if you have any numbness or tingling in the finger, and did you hear a distinct pop or snap at the moment of injury? I need to rule out nerve damage or a subtle ligament tear.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Since the MRI results are pending, let's focus on the specific mechanics: are you able to actively flex the very tip of your finger (the DIP joint) against resistance, or does it remain stuck straight? Please also describe if there is a palpable gap or a visible retraction of the muscle belly near the base of the finger.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the mechanism of injury and the inability to flex the DIP joint, this is clinically a Jersey Finger despite the normal initial ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the absence of neurological symptoms. Based on the mechanism of injury and the inability to actively flex the DIP joint, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus tendon)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
